title: Book object
description: One record per object the book refers to: a definition, theorem, computation, exercise, principle, or open problem. Modelled on axeyum's artifacts/ontology/fact.schema.json: a formal statement AND a status, with evidence whose checker exit status depends on the finding. The book's status boxes are generated from these records and never typed by hand.

id.description: Part letter then a dotted slug. W=Words (Prologue), I=Instructions as functions, C=Cost and certificates, P=Permutations, M=Machines (particular ISAs), OP=open problem.

statement.description: Prose statement, as it appears in the book.

epistemic_status.description: What THIS repository established. 'stated' = a definition or principle with nothing to check.

external_status.description: What the literature or the ISA vendor holds. 'computed-uncertified' = a published exhaustive search with no artifact; 'asserted' = a bare claim in a spec.

scope.description: The declared instruction subset, cost model, width, or other quantifier the claim is relative to. A minimality claim without this field is meaningless.

sha256.description: Map of artifact filename (raw, uncompressed) to SHA-256.

checker_command.description: Run from repo root. MUST exit nonzero when the finding does not hold. Set AXEYUM to an axeyum checkout with prebuilt target/release/examples for solver-backed checks.

negative_control.description: A command that MUST exit nonzero, proving the checker can fail.

reconstruction.description: Whether axeyum can turn this into a kernel theorem with content (TheoryReconstruction) or only attest it (StructuralAttestation).
